issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies Pneumatic.raisePressure(int) returns void, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(int) returning boolean. This return-type mismatch will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and will cause compilation/test failures if tests expect the void signature from the UML/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type of raisePressure(int) between specification and code. Either change the solution (and any tests) so Pneumatic.raisePressure(int) returns void as specified in the UML/problem statement and update all implementing classes accordingly, or update the problem statement/UML and tests to specify a boolean return type if that was intended. Preferably update the interface in the solution to: public interface Pneumatic { void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease); void openValve(); } and adjust implementing classes.
